answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen price, eliminating negotiation (memory_c1/m_c6 paths) and deferral as cost-meeting options. The low-cost vendor's quote alone meets the 18% mandate. Memory_c2 (day 38) records that the prior switch to the low-cost vendor was quick with accurate invoicing — low integration risk. The assembly line is at 94% with no buffer, so any delivery interruption is costly; verifying memory_c2 confirms the vendor's operational track record. Memory_c3 is pulled to assess whether adding a second source for the constrained component is feasible within the same decision, but given the one-decision constraint and the immediate 14-day expiry, the primary action is to switch primary supply to the low-cost vendor. If memory_c2 confirms low onboarding risk and accurate billing, the switch satisfies the cost mandate without materially increasing delivery risk. Memory_c3 verification is secondary: if the constrained component is the one supplied by the incumbent, the switch itself may already diversify; if not, second-sourcing is deferred to next cycle per the one-decision rule.
